_note: Drives the Recipe Graph editor. The tool reads this file to build its creatable-vertex palette, the inspector fields for a selected vertex/edge, the legal wiring matrix, and the invariant list it checks after every mutation — nothing about the node kinds is hardcoded in TypeScript beyond the field-type primitives. Adding a vertex kind or a property is a data edit here, not a code change. Map data files (burger.json, ...) are validated against this.

fieldTypes.note: name of another vertex; refKinds restricts which

mapFields.name: id
mapFields.description: Stable map id, matches the runtime map folder (e.g. "burger").

mapFields.name: gridWidth
mapFields.description: Prep-grid columns. Fixed for every level in the map.

mapFields.name: dirtyStackHeight
mapFields.description: How many dirty objects stack in one grid cell before it overflows and the level is lost.

mapFields.name: visibleRows
mapFields.description: Queue rows shown in Play: 1 interactable front row plus previews.

vertexKinds.label: Ingredient
vertexKinds.description: Any concrete item that can sit in a queue, on the prep grid, or in a dish. A pickupable ingredient is a graph leaf; everything else must be produced by exactly one process edge.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Graph-unique key. Referenced by every edge.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: Shown to designers and players.

fields.name: pickupable
fields.description: Comes off the ingredient queue. Marks this vertex as a graph leaf — a traceback terminates here.

fields.name: servable
fields.description: Can occupy a dish slot. Purely raw items (bun, potato) are not; their processed outputs are.

fields.name: usageNum
fields.description: How many dish slots ONE landed piece can fill before it is consumed. >1 is a shared sauce (chili bowl 2, cheese sauce 3). Note >1 also disables the skip-the-grid direct-serve path in the runtime.

fields.name: limitPerDish
fields.description: Max copies one dish order may call for. 0 = no limit. Bases and one-per-dish toppings use 1.

fields.name: numSlices
fields.description: Sheet-side multiplicity for the raw item. Informational; the authoritative yield is the process edge's `amount`.

fields.name: price
fields.description: Economy value from the ingredient table.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Unity-facing string id.

fields.name: emoji
fields.description: Fallback glyph when no artwork resolves.

fields.name: localImage
fields.description: Bundled asset path relative to src/assets/.

fields.name: fileId
fields.description: Google Drive artwork id.

fields.name: runtimeRawId
fields.description: Id in the map's ingredients table, when this vertex exists there. Kept so a future compiler can round-trip.

fields.name: runtimeCookedId
fields.description: Id in the map's cookedIngredients table, when this vertex exists there.

vertexKinds.label: Tool
vertexKinds.description: A cooking station. Holds numSlots items at once; each finishes after cookingTime seconds. Owns no recipe data itself — each recipe is one outgoing process edge.

fields.name: numSlots
fields.description: How many items cook here simultaneously. The per-tool stack capacity.

fields.name: cookingTime
fields.description: Default seconds per item; a process edge may override it.

fields.name: upgradeCosts
fields.description: Coin cost per upgrade step, indexed from level 1.

vertexKinds.label: Choice group
vertexKinds.description: A reusable choice set referenced as a composite's base or topping, or nested as another group's option. SINGLE picks exactly one option; MULTIPLE picks a multiset.

fields.name: groupType
fields.description: SINGLE = exactly one option, and each option is its own concrete variant. MULTIPLE = any combination, bounded by maxQuantity.

fields.name: maxQuantity
fields.description: Total picks allowed across all options. -1 = unlimited. Ignored for SINGLE. An unlimited MULTIPLE makes the enclosing orderable's variant count unbounded — see the resolver.

vertexKinds.label: Composite
vertexKinds.description: A base plus an optional topping — the assembled thing a customer receives. A composite may itself be another composite's base, so assemblies nest.

fields.name: orderable
fields.description: A customer may order this. Marks a graph root — the tracer starts here.

vertexKinds.label: Dirty object
vertexKinds.description: Left on the prep grid when a customer holding the linked composite leaves. Absent = the map's generic dirty dish.

edgeKinds.label: Processes into
edgeKinds.description: One recipe row: the tool turns `inputs` into the target ingredient. The single most important edge — INV-UNIQUE-PRODUCER caps it at one per target, which is what makes a backward trace deterministic.

fields.name: inputs
fields.description: Ingredients consumed. Modelled as a list so multi-input recipes stay expressible; every current recipe uses exactly one.

fields.name: amount
fields.description: Pieces produced per pickup. A chopping board yielding 2 drops two pieces on the grid at once.

fields.name: duration
fields.description: Overrides the tool's cookingTime for this recipe only.

fields.name: chainTools
fields.description: Extra tools visited in order after the source tool, before the output appears. Produces NO intermediate item and never touches the grid (potato: cutting board, then fryer, then 2 fries).

edgeKinds.label: Base is
edgeKinds.description: What the assembly is built on. Must be present in the dish before any topping can be served onto it.

edgeKinds.label: Topping is
edgeKinds.description: What may go on the base. Optional — a composite with no topping edge is just its base.

edgeKinds.label: Option
edgeKinds.description: One choice within a group. Nesting a group inside a group is legal but must stay acyclic.

fields.name: maxQuantity
fields.description: Max copies of THIS option. -1 = unlimited. Ignored by SINGLE groups.

edgeKinds.label: Leaves behind
edgeKinds.description: The dirty object a served customer leaves. Omit for the map's generic dirty dish.

invariants.description: Every edge endpoint and every ref field names a vertex declared in the same map.
At most one process edge targets any ingredient. An ingredient with no producer must be pickupable.
Vertex names are unique across ALL kinds — base/topping/option edges resolve into one shared namespace.
Every distinct leaf reachable from an orderable composite bottoms out at a pickupable ingredient.
Every composite has exactly one base edge.
Every group has at least one option edge.
Anything reachable as a base or topping leaf is marked servable.
An ingredient produced by a tool but consumed by nothing and not reachable from any orderable.
A pickupable ingredient no orderable reaches.
An orderable's concrete-variant count is unbounded because a MULTIPLE group on its path is uncapped. Expected for build-your-own items; stated so it is a choice, not an accident.
A tool with no process edges.
A SINGLE group with exactly one option.
